article_title: Using mobile technologies for mathematics: effects on student attitudes and achievement
citation: Fabian, K., Topping, K. J., & Barron, I. G. (2018). Using mobile technologies for mathematics: effects on student attitudes and achievement. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-018-9580-3
title: M3 evaluation framework (Micro, Meso, Macro) for mobile learning interventions
description: The study adopts Vavoula and Sharples' (2011) M3 evaluation framework, which provides a "structured format to assess usability, educational and organisational impact and their inter-relationships". Micro-level evaluates individual user experience of the technology via end-activity evaluations; meso-level examines student experience via group and teacher interviews; macro-level evaluates effects on attitudes and performance via pre-post designs with experimental and control groups. The authors report it was "valuable for data validation and triangulation".
requirements: Requires measures at three levels: usability ratings, interviews, and pre-post attitude and achievement tests with a comparison group
examples: The study evaluated tablet usability (micro), student and teacher perceptions (meso), and attitude and test-score effects (macro)
key_sources: Fabian, K., Topping, K. J., & Barron, I. G. (2018). Using mobile technologies for mathematics: effects on student attitudes and achievement. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-018-9580-3

article_title: Myartspace: Design and evaluation of support for learning with multimedia phones between classrooms and museums
citation: Vavoula, G., Sharples, M., Rudman, P., Meek, J., & Lonsdale, P. (2009). Myartspace: Design and evaluation of support for learning with multimedia phones between classrooms and museums. Computers & Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2009.02.007
title: M3 evaluation framework for mobile learning across micro, meso and macro levels
description: The M3 evaluation framework structures evaluation of mobile learning technology at three levels: micro (usability and utility of individual activities), meso (the learning experience as a whole, including learning breakthroughs and breakdowns), and macro (longer-term impact on established educational and learning practice). It operates through a three-stage process of capturing user expectations, capturing reality through observation, and examining gaps between them. The article applies it throughout the Myartspace project lifecycle, from requirements analysis through design, implementation and deployment.
requirements: Evaluation must be integrated throughout the technology development lifecycle rather than conducted as a final 'success or failure' test
constraints: Macro-level evaluation requires that the technology is deployed long enough to assess its impact on practice
target_learning_goals: inquiry learning connecting museum and classroom
examples: Applied to evaluate Myartspace at three pilot sites: the Study Gallery in Poole, Urbis in Manchester, and the D-Day museum in Portsmouth
key_sources: Vavoula, G., Sharples, M., Rudman, P., Meek, J., & Lonsdale, P. (2009). Myartspace: Design and evaluation of support for learning with multimedia phones between classrooms and museums. Computers & Education. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compedu.2009.02.007
